subtitle: When Work Became Worship and Words Became Fire

panels.shot: epic wide of a dim stone hall filled with shadowy figures sitting in a circle, with Basavanna, Akka Mahadevi and Allama Prabhu prominent in the foreground
panels.action: Basavanna stands in simple minister’s robes, Akka Mahadevi draped only in her flowing hair, and Allama Prabhu serene with his drum, all three facing a gathered crowd in a hall lit by oil lamps in Kalyana.

dialogue.text: In twelfth‑century Kalyana, a king’s minister and wandering mystics dared to build a hall where cobbler, woman and Brahmin argued with God as equals: the remembered Anubhava Mantapa of Basavanna and his companions.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं सदी के कल्याण में, एक राजा का मंत्री और घूमते फकीर जुटे—जहाँ मोची, औरत, ब्राह्मण – सब ईश्वर से बराबरी में भिड़े: वही यादों का बसवण्णा का अनुभव मंटपा।

panels.shot: slow push-in on young Basavanna at a village field, low angle with horizon
panels.action: A younger Basavanna, in simple rural clothes, watches peasants and artisans at work in the fields near Basavana Bagewadi under the harsh Deccan sun.

dialogue.text: Basavanna was born in a small town of today’s Karnataka, where the dust of the fields and the smoke of the forges fed a boy who watched work and worship sit in different corners of the village.

i18n.hi: बसवण्णा आज के कर्नाटक के एक कस्बे में जन्मा, खेत की धूल और भट्ठी के धुएँ में पलता वो लड़का, जो देखता कि काम और पूजा गाँव में दो कोनों में बैठे हैं।

panels.shot: medium wide of Kudalasangama river confluence at sunrise, contemplative framing
panels.action: Basavanna stands by the meeting of rivers at Kudalasangama, holding a small ishtalinga in his palm, water mist rising around him.

dialogue.text: At Kudalasangama, under the quiet gaze of stone shrines, he turned inward, taking the ishtalinga onto his own body, seeking a Lord who did not ask for birth-names or priestly fees.

i18n.hi: कूडलसंगम में, पत्थर के मंदिरों की शांत नज़र के नीचे, वह भीतर मुड़ा; इष्टलिंग अपने शरीर पर धारण कर, ऐसे भगवान को खोजता जो न जात पूछे, न पुरोहित की फीस।

panels.shot: interior wide of a royal court, with Basavanna small in the grand space
panels.action: In the Kalachuri court at Kalyana, King Bijjala II sits on a raised throne while Basavanna, now slightly older and more composed, stands among other ministers dressed in modest yet clean robes.

dialogue.text: The Arjunavad inscription and later memories place him in the court of Bijjala II at Kalyana, a minister handling royal wealth in a world where power sat with kings, Brahmins and guilds.

i18n.hi: अर्जुनवाड शिलालेख और बाद की स्मृतियाँ उसे कल्याण के बिज्जल द्वितीय के दरबार में रखती हैं—एक मंत्री, जो उस दुनिया की राज-धन संभालता है जहाँ ताकत राजा, ब्राह्मण और संघों के हाथ में है।

panels.shot: medium on Basavanna discreetly giving coins to a poor artisan outside the court gate
panels.action: Basavanna, stepping out of the palace, quietly hands a pouch of coins to a weary-looking cobbler seated by the roadside, while the city walls loom behind them.

dialogue.text: From this seat near the treasury, Basavanna bent the flow of gifts: not only to temples but to hungry craftsmen and wandering devotees, turning royal coin toward a different kind of order.

i18n.hi: खज़ाने के इसी पास के आसन से बसवण्णा ने दान की धारा मोड़ दी: सिर्फ़ मंदिर नहीं, भूखे कारीगर और घूमते भक्त भी; राजकोष को एक नई व्यवस्था की ओर बहाया।

panels.shot: intimate interior wide of a modest hall with Basavanna addressing a mixed group
panels.action: In a simple pillared hall in Kalyana, Basavanna speaks to a small circle of men and women of different dress and status, some with tools at their side, some with scriptures, all seated on the same floor.

dialogue.text: Here began what would be remembered as the Anubhava Mantapa: not a stone parliament, but a gathered experience, an assembly where weavers, potters, Brahmins and women shared their visions in plain Kannada.

i18n.hi: यहीं शुरू हुई जो अनुभव मंटपा के नाम से याद रही: पत्थर की संसद नहीं, जुड़ा हुआ अनुभव—जहाँ जुलाहा, कुम्हार, ब्राह्मण, और औरतें साधी कन्नड़ में अपने दर्शन बाँटते।

panels.shot: close-up on Basavanna’s hands holding tools and the ishtalinga together
panels.action: Basavanna sits cross-legged, one hand resting on a carpenter’s chisel and the other cradling the small ishtalinga, his face intent.

dialogue.text: In vachanas later remembered in Harihara’s ragales and Ramanujan’s pages, his voice made kayaka, one’s work, into worship, and the body’s labour into a temple that needed no caste-marked doorway.

i18n.hi: इन वचनों को बाद में हरिहर की रगले और रामानुजन की किताबों में याद किया गया—उसकी आवाज़ ने ‘कायक’, अपना काम, को पूजा बना दिया; शरीर की मेहनत को ऐसा मंदिर, जिसे किसी जाति के चिह्न वाले दरवाज़े की ज़रूरत नहीं।

panels.shot: dramatic entrance shot of Allama Prabhu into the hall, low angle with shadow
panels.action: Allama Prabhu, lean and calm, steps into the hall with his small drum in hand, his eyes distant, as the gathered sharanas turn to look at him with curiosity.

dialogue.text: From the caves and streets came others: Allama Prabhu, remembered as a drummer-ascetic, whose spare, riddling vachanas cut through pride, and who would sit at the heart of this debating circle.

i18n.hi: गुफाओं और गलियों से और भी आए: अल्लामा प्रभु—ढोलक-योगी के रूप में याद, जिनके सूखे, पहेलीनुमा वचन घमंड चीर देते, और जो इस बहस के गोले के बीचोंबीच बैठते।

panels.shot: medium on Allama and Basavanna sitting opposite, calm but intense
panels.action: Allama Prabhu and Basavanna sit facing each other in the hall, surrounded by attentive sharanas, their postures relaxed yet charged as if in deep exchange.

dialogue.speaker: basavanna_akka_mahadevi_and_allama_prabhu
dialogue.text: “Let the tongue speak only what the work has lived.”

i18n.hi: "जीभ वही बोले, जो काम ने जीया हो।"

panels.shot: wide shot of Akka Mahadevi entering the Mantapa, hair flowing, crowd reacting
panels.action: Akka Mahadevi walks into the hall, unclothed but covered by her long, loose hair, her eyes fierce and inward, as some in the circle look shocked while others bow in respect.

dialogue.text: And Akka Mahadevi, whose life is sung in many later accounts, entered this remembered circle covered only by her hair and her devotion, her vachanas calling Shiva her only husband and earthly ties a distraction.

i18n.hi: और अक्का महादेवी—जिसकी कथा बाद की कई कहानियों में गाई गई—यह यादों की सभा में दाख़िल हुई, सिर्फ़ बाल और भक्ति में ढकी; उसके वचन शिव को अकेला पति कहते, बाकी सारे रिश्ते बंधन।

panels.shot: close-up on Akka Mahadevi’s intense face as she speaks, background softened
panels.action: Akka Mahadevi sits composed among the men, face glowing with conviction as she addresses them, while Allama and Basavanna listen closely.

dialogue.speaker: basavanna_akka_mahadevi_and_allama_prabhu
dialogue.text: “Why bind the sky in a house of walls?”

i18n.hi: "आसमान को दीवारों के घर में क्यों बाँधते हो?"

panels.shot: dynamic wide of the Mantapa in full session, with diverse figures speaking in turn
panels.action: The hall is now crowded: a cobbler, a washerman, a Brahmin, a woman with a child, and others sit in a circle, one after another rising to speak as Basavanna, Allama, and Akka listen among them.

dialogue.text: Within a generation, hundreds of sharanas—names preserved across the vachana collections—voiced their experience, arguing, contradicting, singing in Kannada prose-poems that carried the heat of the street into the language of God.

i18n.hi: एक ही पीढ़ी में, सैकड़ों शरण—जिनके नाम वचन-संग्रहों में बिखरे हैं—अपने अनुभव बोले; भिड़े, उलटे, गाए, कन्नड़ गद्य-कविताओं में, जो सड़क की गरमी को भगवान की भाषा में ले आए।

panels.shot: medium on Basavanna gently refusing a priestly ritual offering, with a small gathering watching
panels.action: A temple priest offers a ritual plate toward Basavanna, who smiles politely and declines with a slight bow, while a few artisans and officials observe the exchange.

dialogue.text: Ishtalinga on their bodies, they loosened the old knots of temple and birth; yet even as they questioned Brahmin ritual, many still carried the habits of their world, and caste did not vanish from twelfth‑century Karnataka overnight.

i18n.hi: शरीर पर इष्टलिंग के साथ, उन्होंने मंदिर और जन्म के पुराने गाँठ ढीले किए; फिर भी, जैसे वे ब्राह्मण रीति पर सवाल उठाते, वैसे ही अपने ज़माने की आदतें भी ढोते रहे—जात बारहवीं सदी के कर्नाटक से रातों-रात नहीं गई।

panels.shot: tense interior of the court, with Brahmins and elites confronting Bijjala and Basavanna
panels.action: In the royal court, Brahmin scholars and offended elites stand before King Bijjala, gesturing in complaint, while Basavanna stands to one side, calm but troubled.

dialogue.text: The king’s court, caught between revenue, ritual and revolt, heard complaints: that the minister’s circle ignored rank, that artisans dared debate Brahmins, that social walls were being thinned in the very capital.

i18n.hi: राजदरबार, जहाँ राजस्व, पूजा और बगावत की रस्सियाँ खिंच रही थीं, शिकायतें सुनता रहा: कि मंत्री की मंडली ऊँच-नीच को मानती नहीं; कि कारीगर ब्राह्मणों से बहस करने की जुर्रत करते; कि राजधानी में ही दीवारें पतली हो रही हैं।

panels.shot: somber wide of Kalyana streets with soldiers and frightened townsfolk, distant fires
panels.action: Soldiers move through Kalyana’s narrow streets as townsfolk watch anxiously from doorways; smoke rises in the distance, hinting at unrest.

dialogue.text: Traditions, hagiographies and history agree at least on this: tension rose. A royal order, a marriage across caste lines, a clash of loyalties—details differ, but by the late 1160s, Kalyana was no longer at peace.

i18n.hi: कथाएँ, भक्ति-चरित और इतिहास कम से कम इस बात पर सहमत हैं: तनातनी बढ़ी। एक शाही फरमान, एक अंतरजाति विवाह, निष्ठाओं की टक्कर—ब्योरे अलग हैं, पर 1160 के दशक के अंत तक कल्याण शांत नहीं रहा।

panels.shot: medium of Basavanna leaving the city gate, looking back once
panels.action: Basavanna walks out of Kalyana’s gate with a small bundle, turning briefly to look back at the city walls as a few sharanas watch in sorrow.

dialogue.text: Later Virashaiva memory tells that Basavanna left Kalyana and returned toward Kudalasangama, his experiment shaken by royal displeasure and conflict, his body’s path ending while his words travelled on.

i18n.hi: बाद की वीरशैव स्मृति कहती है कि बसवण्णा कल्याण छोड़, फिर कूडलसंगम की ओर लौटा—उसका प्रयोग राज-अप्रसाद और टकराव से हिल चुका; शरीर की राह थमी, पर उसके शब्द चलते रहे।

panels.shot: poignant shot of Allama seated alone in a dim corner of the hall, the space half-empty
panels.action: Allama Prabhu sits alone in the now sparsely filled hall, oil lamps burning low, his drum resting beside him, as his gaze falls on the empty places where companions once sat.

i18n.hi: "आवाज़ें बिखर जाती हैं, गूँज ठहर जाती है।"

panels.shot: transitional montage wide of scribes and devotees across time copying vachanas
panels.action: A visual montage shows later scribes and devotees across centuries in different dress, sitting with palm-leaf manuscripts, copying and reciting vachanas attributed to Basavanna, Akka Mahadevi, Allama and other sharanas.

dialogue.text: Over the next centuries, their vachanas were gathered, edited and argued over; Virashaiva and Lingayat communities traced roots to them, while scholars still debate where Basavanna’s hand began and where older currents flowed in.

i18n.hi: अगली सदियों में उनके वचन जुटाए गए, सँवारे गए, और खुद पर बहस हुई; वीरशैव और लिंगायत जनसमुदायों ने अपनी जड़ें उनमें जोड़ी, और विद्वान अब भी टटोलते हैं कि बसवण्णा का हाथ कहाँ से शुरू होता है, और पुरानी धाराएँ कहाँ से मिलती हैं।

panels.shot: final wide shot of a modern gathering in a simple hall, faint silhouettes of Basavanna, Akka and Allama behind them
panels.action: A present-day group of men and women in contemporary clothes sit in a circle in a bare hall, sharing and listening, while ghostly, respectful silhouettes of Basavanna, Akka Mahadevi and Allama Prabhu loom softly in the background.

dialogue.text: In the remembered Parliament of Souls at Kalyana, they did not erase hierarchy in a day, but they dared to stage a different conversation—and each time we let a cobbler’s, a woman’s, a mystic’s voice stand, their Mantapa flickers back to life.

i18n.hi: कल्याण की उस यादों की संसद में, उन्होंने एक दिन में ऊँच-नीच नहीं मिटाई; पर एक नई बातचीत का मंच ज़रूर खड़ा किया—और जब भी हम मोची, औरत या फकीर की आवाज़ को खड़ा रहने देते हैं, उनका मंटपा फिर से झिलमिल उठता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: When Work Became Worship and Words Became Fire
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब काम पूजा बना, और शब्द अंगार
